subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$, and for a finite set $S$ of indices let $X_S$ be the set of tuples
$x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} X_i$ with $x_i \in U_i$ for every $i \notin S$. If $S \subseteq T$ are
finite sets of indices, then $X_S \subseteq X_T$.

articles.title: Piece of a restricted product supported in a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a
family of types with subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$. For a finite set $S$ of indices, the piece
$X_S$ is the set of tuples $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} X_i$ such that $x_i \in U_i$ for every
$i \notin S$.

articles.title: Krull dimension drops on proper closed subsets of irreducible sets
articles.statement:
A proper closed subset of an irreducible set has Krull dimension at
least one less than the ambient set.

articles.title: Distortion ratio
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$,
the distortion ratio of $K$ at $s$ and $t$ is the intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ along $K$
divided by the Euclidean distance $\lVert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rVert$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where
division by $0$ gives $0$.

articles.title: Distortion of a knot
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$, the distortion of $K$ is the supremum in the
extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ of the distortion ratios of $K$ at $s$ and $t$, taken
over all distinct parameters $s \ne t$ in the half-open interval $[0, 2\pi)$.

articles.title: Intrinsic distance on a knot
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, let $\ell$ be the
arc length of $K$ between the parameters $s$ and $t$, and let $L$ be the total arc length of $K$.
The intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ is $\min(\ell, L - \ell)$. When $s$ and $t$ lie in one
closed interval of length $2\pi$, this is the length of the shorter of the two arcs of $K$ joining
the points with parameters $s$ and $t$.

articles.title: Arc length between two parameters
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and real
numbers $s$ and $t$, the arc length of $K$ between $s$ and $t$ is
$\left| \int_s^t \lVert \gamma'(u) \rVert \, du \right|$, the length of the arc that $\gamma$ traces
between the parameters $s$ and $t$. It does not depend on the order of $s$ and $t$.

articles.title: Pardon's lower bound for the distortion of torus knots
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime positive
integers, let $T_{p,q}$ be the standard $(p, q)$-torus curve, and let $K$ be a knot with
parametrization $\gamma$. Suppose there are an ambient isotopy $H$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$, with
time-one map $H_1$, and a strictly increasing diffeomorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{R}$ with
$\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for all real $t$, such that
$H_1(\gamma(t)) = T_{p,q}(\sigma(t))$ for every real $t$. Then the distortion of $K$ is at least
$\min(p, q)/160$.

This is the smooth, oriented specialization of Pardon's theorem, which bounds the distortion of
every rectifiable curve in the knot type of the $(p, q)$-torus knot.

## Sources

- John Pardon, 'On the distortion of knots on embedded surfaces', Annals of Mathematics (2) 174 (2011), no. 1, 637-646, Theorem 1.1. https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2011.174.1.21. Problem `pardon_torus_knot_distortion` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Speed of a knot
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and a real number $t$,
the speed of $K$ at $t$ is the Euclidean norm $\lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert$ of the derivative of
$\gamma$ at $t$.

articles.title: Standard torus curve
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, the standard $(p, q)$-torus curve is
the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ sending $t$ to
$((2 + \cos qt) \cos pt,\ (2 + \cos qt) \sin pt,\ \sin qt)$. It lies on the torus of revolution
about the $z$-axis with major radius $2$ and minor radius $1$, and as $t$ runs over $[0, 2\pi]$ it
winds $p$ times around the $z$-axis and $q$ times around the core circle of the torus.

articles.title: Total arc length of a knot
articles.statement:
For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$, the total arc
length of $K$ is the arc length of $K$ between the parameters $0$ and $2\pi$, namely
$\left| \int_0^{2\pi} \lVert \gamma'(u) \rVert \, du \right|$.

articles.title: Existence of a chiral knot
articles.statement:
There exists an oriented smooth knot $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$
that is chiral: it is not ambient-isotopic, as an oriented knot, to its mirror image $r \circ K$,
where $r(x, y, z) = (x, y, -z)$ is the reflection through the $xy$-plane.

## Sources

- Classical; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chirality_(mathematics) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trefoil_knot. Problem `exists_chiral_knot` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Links with a crossing-free regular projection admit alternating diagrams
articles.statement:
If a
parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then
$L$ admits an alternating diagram.

The witness is $L$ itself, whose projection is alternating vacuously since it has no crossings.

articles.title: Links admitting an alternating diagram
articles.statement:
A parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components admits
an alternating diagram when there is a parametrized link $L'$ isotopic to $L$ whose standard
projection is regular and alternating.

articles.title: Number of components of a dart diagram
articles.statement:
The number of components of a dart diagram $D$ is
the number of classes of darts of $D$ under unoriented strand connectivity, plus the recorded
number of isolated crossingless components of $D$.

articles.title: Strand-connectivity relation on darts
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, this is the equivalence
relation on the darts of $D$ generated by relating each dart $d$ to its partner across an edge
segment and to the opposite dart of $d$ at the same crossing. Two darts are related exactly when
they lie on the same unoriented strand component.

articles.title: Crossing count of a regular projection
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ whose standard
projection is regular, the crossing count of $L$ is the number of crossings of the projection,
that is, the number of points of its double-point set.

Regularity guarantees that the double-point set is finite, and the value does not depend on the
chosen proof of regularity.

articles.title: A crossing-free regular projection has crossing count zero
articles.statement:
If a parametrized link $L$ has
a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then the crossing count of $L$ is
$0$.

articles.title: A regular projection with a crossing has positive crossing count
articles.statement:
If a parametrized link
$L$ has a regular standard projection with at least one crossing, then the crossing count of $L$
is positive.

articles.title: Number of crossings of a dart diagram
articles.statement:
The crossing count of a dart diagram $D$ is the
number of vertices of $D$, each vertex being one crossing.

articles.title: The crossing number is an isotopy invariant
articles.statement:
If two parametrized links $L_1$ and $L_2$ with
$n$ components are isotopic, then $L_1$ and $L_2$ have the same crossing number.

articles.title: Crossing number zero from a crossing-free representative
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized
links with $n$ components such that $L'$ is isotopic to $L$. If the standard projection of $L'$ is
regular and its double-point set is empty, then the crossing number of $L$ is $0$.

articles.title: Regular projections of isotopic links bound the crossing number
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $L'$ be
oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components, with $L'$ ambient isotopic to $L$, and
suppose the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular. Then the crossing number of $L$
is at most the number of crossings of this projection of $L'$.

articles.title: A link's own regular projection bounds its crossing number
articles.statement:
If the standard projection of
an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of
$L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection.

articles.title: Finiteness of the crossing number
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links
with $n$ components. If $L'$ is ambient isotopic to $L$ and the standard projection of $L'$ to
the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is finite.

articles.title: Crossing number of a link
articles.statement:
For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$
components, the crossing number of $L$ is the infimum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, over all
parametrized links $L'$ with $n$ components that are ambient isotopic to $L$ and whose standard
projection to the plane is regular, of the number of crossings (double points) of that
projection of $L'$. It is $\infty$ when no such $L'$ exists.

Changing the projection direction is absorbed by varying the representative over its isotopy
class.

articles.title: Crossings of a link projection
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. A
crossing of $L$ is a point of the double-point set of $L$, that is, a point $p$ of the plane
$\mathbb{R}^2$ such that two distinct parameter points of $L$ both have image $p$ under the
standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.

articles.title: Cyclically adjacent crossing preimages
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be an oriented labeled parametrized link,
with each component parametrized by $t \in [0, 2\pi)$. Two distinct parameter points $a$ and $b$
of $L$ on the same component are cyclically adjacent, in this order, when both are crossing
preimages (they project to double points of the standard projection) and no crossing preimage on
that component lies in the open arc from $a$ to $b$ in the direction of increasing parameter,
wrapping around from $2\pi$ to $0$ when the parameter of $b$ is smaller than that of $a$.

articles.title: Dart diagram
articles.statement:
A dart diagram consists of a finite set $V$ of crossings, a
fixed-point-free involution $\mathrm{pair}$ of the set $V \times \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ of darts, and a
natural number counting isolated crossingless components.

Darts $0, 1, 2, 3$ at a crossing are read in counterclockwise order, darts $0$ and $2$ form the
over-strand and darts $1$ and $3$ the under-strand, and $\mathrm{pair}$ glues darts across edge
segments. The structure does not by itself assert planarity.

articles.title: Darts of a dart diagram
articles.statement:
The darts of a dart diagram $D$ with crossing set $V$ are the
pairs $(v, i)$ with $v \in V$ and $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; the dart $(v, i)$ is the $i$-th
incident half-edge at the crossing $v$.

articles.title: Double points of a link projection
articles.statement:
For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with
$n$ components, the double-point set of $L$ is the set of points $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$
for which there are two distinct parameter points of $L$ (each a component index together with a
parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) whose images under the standard projection, which forgets the third
coordinate, both equal $p$.

articles.title: Empty dart diagram
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$, the empty dart diagram with $k$ isolated
components has no crossings, hence no darts, and records $k$ isolated crossingless components.

It is alternating, since the alternating condition is vacuous when there are no darts.

articles.title: The over and under preimages exhaust a crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$
components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection.
Every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is either the over-strand preimage or
the under-strand preimage of $p$.

articles.title: Double points have exactly two preimages
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$
components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a point of the double-point set
of $L$. Then there are parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ whose projected points are both $p$, and
every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is $a$ or $b$.

articles.title: The over-strand preimage exists and is unique
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$
components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection.
There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an over-strand preimage of $p$: the
projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has
height strictly less than the height of $a$.

articles.title: The under-strand preimage exists and is unique
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$
components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection.
There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an under-strand preimage of $p$: the
projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has
height strictly greater than the height of $a$.

articles.title: Points with the same projection have different heights
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link
with $n$ components. If two distinct parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ have the same projected
point, then the heights of $L$ at $a$ and at $b$ are different.

This is forced by component injectivity in one period and pairwise disjoint component traces;
over/under is therefore derived from the parametrization rather than chosen.

articles.title: The under-strand lies strictly below the over-strand
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with
$n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that
projection. The height of $L$ at the under-strand preimage of $p$ is strictly less than its
height at the over-strand preimage of $p$.

articles.title: Height of a parameter point
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and a
parameter point $a$ of $L$, the height of $L$ at $a$ is the height (the third coordinate) of
the point of Euclidean 3-space that $a$ represents on $L$.

articles.title: Height in the standard projection frame
articles.statement:
The height of a point
$x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$ of Euclidean 3-space is its third coordinate $x_3$.

articles.title: The projected trace is the union of the projected components
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link
$L$ with $n$ components, the union over all components $i$ of the images of the projected curves
of $L$ equals the image of the trace of $L$ under the standard projection to the plane.

articles.title: Open arc on the parameter circle
articles.statement:
Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be parameter points with parameters
$s$, $u$, $t \in [0, 2\pi)$ respectively. Then $c$ lies in the open counterclockwise arc from $a$
to $b$ when $s < t < u$ in case $s < u$, and when $s < t$ or $t < u$ in case $u \le s$. Only the
parameters are compared; the components of $a$, $b$, $c$ play no role.

articles.title: Crossingless regular projections are alternating
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose
standard projection to the plane is regular. If the double-point set of this projection is empty,
then the projection is alternating.

articles.title: Alternating regular projections
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection
to the plane is regular. The projection is alternating when, for any two cyclically adjacent
crossing preimages $a$ and $b$ of $L$ (distinct, on the same component, with no other crossing
preimage of that component in the open arc of parameters from $a$ to $b$), the over/under status
at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.

A component with at most one crossing preimage imposes no condition.

articles.title: Alternating dart diagrams
articles.statement:
A dart diagram is alternating when, for every dart $d$, the
dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$, reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and going straight
through the next crossing, has the opposite over/under status to $d$. In other words, consecutive
crossings on every strand have opposite over/under status.

Crossingless components impose no condition.

articles.title: Crossing preimages
articles.statement:
A parameter point $a$ of a parametrized link $L$ (a component of $L$
together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) is a crossing preimage when its image under the
standard projection to the plane lies in the double-point set of $L$.

articles.title: The two preimages of a crossing have opposite status
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link
whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If $a \ne b$ are crossing preimages of $L$ with
the same projection, then the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.

articles.title: Over/under status at a crossing preimage
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard
projection to the plane is regular, and let $a$ be a crossing preimage of $L$. The over/under
status at $a$ is true when $a$ is the over-strand preimage of the crossing at the projection of
$a$, that is, the preimage of that crossing of greatest height, and false otherwise.

articles.title: Being the over-strand preimage of a crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a
crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an over point
of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly
smaller height than $a$.

articles.title: Over-strand darts
articles.statement:
The four darts at a crossing of a dart diagram carry the labels
$0, 1, 2, 3$ in cyclic order. A dart lies on the over-strand at its crossing when its label is
$0$ or $2$.

articles.title: Regular projections
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link; a parameter point of $L$ is a
component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$. The standard projection of $L$ to the
plane, which forgets the third coordinate, is regular when the following hold: at every parameter
point, the projection of the velocity vector of the component curve is nonzero; the double-point
set is finite; no three pairwise distinct parameter points have the same projection; and at any
two distinct parameter points with the same projection, the projected velocity vectors are
linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$.

The condition records no diagram, crossing labels or over/under data. The heights at two distinct
parameter points with the same projection always differ, because each component is injective on
a period and the components are pairwise disjoint.

articles.title: Being the under-strand preimage of a crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a
crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an under point
of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly
greater height than $a$.

articles.title: Isolated components are counted in the component count
articles.statement:
For every dart diagram $D$,
the number of isolated crossingless components recorded in $D$ is at most the number of
components of $D$.

articles.title: Strand traversal permutation
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, the strand traversal permutation
of the darts of $D$ is the edge-pairing permutation followed by the opposite-dart permutation:
it sends a dart $d$ to the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where
$\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$.

articles.title: Strand traversal step
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d$ of $D$, the next dart
after $d$ is the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is
the edge-pairing involution of $D$: cross the edge segment at $d$, then go straight through
the crossing reached.

articles.title: Admitting an alternating diagram is an isotopy invariant
articles.statement:
Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be
parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ and $L_1$ admits an
alternating diagram, then $L_2$ admits an alternating diagram.

articles.title: Opposite-dart permutation
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, the opposite-dart permutation of the
darts of $D$ is the square of the quarter-turn rotation permutation: it sends the dart $(v, i)$
at crossing $v$ to the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.

articles.title: Opposite dart
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d = (v, i)$ of $D$, the opposite dart
is obtained by rotating $d$ twice counterclockwise around its crossing $v$; it is the dart
$(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.

articles.title: Over-strand preimage of a crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components
whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The
over-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and
such that every other parameter point projecting to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.

articles.title: Edge-pairing permutation
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, the edge-pairing permutation is the
edge-pairing involution of $D$ regarded as a permutation of the darts of $D$; it is its own
inverse.

articles.title: Parameter point
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, a parameter point consists of a component
index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a real parameter $t$ with $0 \le t < 2\pi$, the fundamental
half-open period. It represents the point at parameter $t$ of component $i$ of a parametrized
link with $n$ components.

articles.title: Standard projection to the plane
articles.statement:
The standard projection sends a point
$x = (x_0, x_1, x_2)$ of Euclidean 3-space to the point $(x_0, x_1)$ of the Euclidean plane,
forgetting the third coordinate.

articles.title: Point of a link at a parameter point
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ with components
$\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point
$a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the point of $L$ at $a$ is
$\gamma_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$.

articles.title: Projected curve of a link component
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ with components
$\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and $i < n$, the projected curve
of component $i$ is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$, $t \mapsto \pi(\gamma_i(t))$, where
$\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ is the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.

articles.title: The over-strand preimage lies over its crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose
standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the
double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the over-strand parameter point
at $p$ is $p$.

articles.title: The under-strand preimage lies over its crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose
standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the
double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the under-strand parameter point
at $p$ is $p$.

articles.title: Projected point of a link at a parameter point
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ with
components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point
$a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the projected point of $L$ at $a$ is
$\pi(\gamma_i(t)) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ forgets the third
coordinate.

articles.title: Euclidean plane
articles.statement:
The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm, the
target plane of the fixed standard projection frame.

articles.title: Rotation permutation of darts
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation permutation is the
permutation of the darts of $D$ sending a dart $(v, i)$, with $v$ a crossing and
$i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, to $(v, i + 1)$; its inverse sends $(v, i)$ to $(v, i - 1)$.

articles.title: Rotation of a dart
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation of a dart $(v, i)$ of $D$, with
$v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, is the dart $(v, i + 1)$: one step counterclockwise
around the crossing $v$.

articles.title: A traversal step stays in the same component
articles.statement:
For every dart $d$ of a dart diagram $D$,
the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$ reached by one step of strand traversal lies in the same
component as $d$.

articles.title: Same component relation on darts
articles.statement:
For a dart diagram $D$, two darts of $D$ lie in the
same component when they are related by the equivalence relation on darts generated by
$d \sim \operatorname{pair}(d)$, crossing an edge segment, and $d \sim \operatorname{opposite}(d)$,
going straight through a crossing.

The oriented traversal $\operatorname{next}$ traverses every component twice, once in each
orientation, so the cycles of the traversal permutation are not themselves the components.

articles.title: A traversal step stays in its strand cycle
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be a dart diagram, and for a dart
$d$ of $D$ let $\operatorname{next}(d)$ be the dart reached from $d$ by crossing its edge
segment and then going straight through the next crossing. Then for every dart $d$ of $D$, the
darts $d$ and $\operatorname{next}(d)$ lie in the same cycle of the strand traversal
permutation of $D$, the permutation of the darts of $D$ that sends each dart $e$ to
$\operatorname{next}(e)$.

articles.title: Projected tangent vector
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link and let $a$ be a parameter point
of $L$, given by a component $i$ and a parameter $t$. The projected tangent vector of $L$ at $a$
is the vector of $\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained by applying the standard projection
$(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y)$ to the derivative $\gamma_i'(t)$ of the curve $\gamma_i$ of the
$i$-th component of $L$ at $t$.

This is the projection of the ambient derivative; it is not defined as the derivative of the
projected curve.

articles.title: Over and under preimages differ
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection
is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. Then the under-strand preimage of $p$
and the over-strand preimage of $p$ are distinct parameter points of $L$.

articles.title: Under-strand preimage of a crossing
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard
projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. The under-strand preimage
of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and whose height is strictly
less than the height of every other parameter point projecting to $p$; the height of a parameter
point is the third coordinate of the corresponding point of $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

articles.title: Smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$
articles.statement:
A smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$
consists of two families of maps $H_t, G_t \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ indexed by
$t \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ and $(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ are smooth
($C^\infty$) maps $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, $G_t$ is a two-sided inverse
of $H_t$ for every $t$, and $H_0$ is the identity. In particular every $H_t$ is a
diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$.

articles.title: Smooth ambient isotopy of Euclidean 3-space
articles.statement:
A smooth ambient isotopy of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ consists of two families of maps $H_t, G_t \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$,
indexed by times $t \in \mathbb{R}$, such that $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ and
$(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ are $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^3$, $G_t(H_t(x)) = x$
and $H_t(G_t(x)) = x$ for all $t$ and $x$, and $H_0$ is the identity.

articles.title: Tracing a strand through one crossing
articles.statement:
Let a traversal state consist of a current
strand position $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list of vertices in $\mathbb{R}^3$, let
$w \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a braid generator with $i = |w|$, and let
$z_{\mathrm{top}}, z_{\mathrm{bot}} \in \mathbb{R}$. Put
$z_{\mathrm{hi}} = z_{\mathrm{top}} - (z_{\mathrm{top}} - z_{\mathrm{bot}})/4$ and
$z_{\mathrm{lo}} = z_{\mathrm{bot}} + (z_{\mathrm{top}} - z_{\mathrm{bot}})/4$. The new state is
obtained by changing the position and appending the listed points, in order, to the vertex
list. If $p = i$ and $w > 0$, the new position is $i + 1$ and the points are
$(i, 1, z_{\mathrm{hi}})$, $(i + 1, 1, z_{\mathrm{lo}})$, $(i + 1, 0, z_{\mathrm{bot}})$. If
$p = i$ and $w \le 0$, the new position is $i + 1$ and the only point is
$(i + 1, 0, z_{\mathrm{bot}})$. If $p = i + 1$ and $w > 0$, the new position is $i$ and the
only point is $(i, 0, z_{\mathrm{bot}})$. If $p = i + 1$ and $w \le 0$, the new position is
$i$ and the points are $(i + 1, 1, z_{\mathrm{hi}})$, $(i, 1, z_{\mathrm{lo}})$,
$(i, 0, z_{\mathrm{bot}})$. Otherwise the position stays $p$ and the only point is
$(p, 0, z_{\mathrm{bot}})$.

The step is meant for $z_{\mathrm{bot}} < z_{\mathrm{top}}$, with the crossing in the slab
between these heights: the strand passing over is lifted to $y = 1$, and the strand passing
under stays at $y = 0$.

articles.title: Tracing a strand through a braid word
articles.statement:
Given a traversal state $s$, a braid word
$w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ (a list of integers) and a starting index $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the
one-crossing step is applied to the state for each generator in turn, starting from $s$: the
generator $w_j$ is applied with top height $-(k + j)$ and bottom height $-(k + j + 1)$. The
result is the final state; for the empty word it is $s$.

articles.title: Polyline closure of a braid word
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let
$w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ be a braid word (a list of integers, where $i > 0$ stands for
$\sigma_i$ and $-i$ for $\sigma_i^{-1}$). If $m = 0$, the value is the junk list $(0, 0, 0)$,
$(1, 0, 0)$, $(0, 1, 0)$. Otherwise the value is a list of vertices in $\mathbb{R}^3$ tracing the
closure of $w$ as one polyline component. It starts at the vertex $(1, 0, 0)$ on strand position
$1$ and makes passes through the braid: in each pass the crossing $w_j$ occupies the slab between
heights $z = -(j + 1)$ and $z = -j$, with the strand passing over lifted to $y = 1$, and each
pass is followed by a closure arc through $y = 100$ back up to height $z = 0$. Tracing stops as
soon as a pass ends at position $1$, or after $n$ passes.

The layout is designed for words with $1 \le |w_j| \le n - 1$ for every $j$, where the strands
sit at the $x$-positions $1, \dots, n$; other words still yield a vertex list, but not a
meaningful one.

articles.title: Chiral knot
articles.statement:
Let $K \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be an oriented smooth knot, and
let $\rho(x, y, z) = (x, y, -z)$ be the reflection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ through the $xy$-plane.
Call $\sigma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ an orientation-preserving reparametrization of
the circle if it is a strictly increasing smooth bijection with smooth inverse satisfying
$\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, that is, the lift of an
orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R} / 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$. The knot $K$ is chiral
if there is no smooth ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ together with such a $\sigma$
satisfying $H_1(K(t)) = \rho(K(\sigma(t)))$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$. Equivalently, $K$ is
not ambient isotopic, as an oriented knot, to its mirror image $\rho \circ K$.

articles.title: Unit circle in the plane
articles.statement:
The unit Euclidean circle
$\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \mid x^2 + y^2 = 1\}$, the source of the boundary of
a slicing disk.

articles.title: Orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle
articles.statement:
An orientation-preserving
smooth reparametrization of the circle is given by maps $f, g \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$,
both $C^\infty$ and inverse to each other ($g(f(t)) = t$ and $f(g(t)) = t$ for all $t$), such
that $f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, and $f$ is
strictly increasing. Here $f$ is a lift of the reparametrization and $g$ is a lift of its
inverse.

articles.title: Composition of circle reparametrizations
articles.statement:
If $\sigma$ and $\tau$ are circle
reparametrizations with lifts $f_\sigma, f_\tau$ and inverse lifts $g_\sigma, g_\tau$, their
composition (first $\sigma$, then $\tau$) is the circle reparametrization with lift
$f_\tau \circ f_\sigma$ and inverse lift $g_\sigma \circ g_\tau$.

articles.title: Composition of ambient isotopies
articles.statement:
If $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are smooth ambient isotopies of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ with forward families $H_t, H'_t$ and inverse families $G_t, G'_t$, their
composition (first $\Phi$, then $\Psi$, at the same time parameter) is the ambient isotopy
with forward family $H'_t \circ H_t$ and inverse family $G_t \circ G'_t$.

articles.title: Braid word for the Conway knot
articles.statement:
The braid word
$\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^{2}$
on $4$ strands, encoded as the list of integers $[-1, -1, 2, -1, 2, -1, 3, -2, -2, 3, 3]$, where
an entry $i > 0$ stands for the generator $\sigma_i$ and $-i$ for $\sigma_i^{-1}$. It has
length $11$ and writhe $-1$, and is a braid word for the Conway knot 11n34.

## Sources

- KnotInfo's `11n_34` record, `braid_notation` field. The Knot Atlas records a different but Markov-equivalent presentation for the same knot, `[1, 1, 2, -3, 2, 1, -3, -2, -2, -3, -3]` (which it labels `K11n34`, the mirror of the Conway knot); both representations agree on braid index 4, braid length 11, and writhe `-1`. Sliceness is mirror-invariant, so either braid word is a valid witness for `conway_knot_not_smoothly_slice`.

articles.title: The Conway knot
articles.statement:
The Conway knot 11n34 as a piecewise-linear closed polyline in
$\mathbb{R}^3$: its vertices are those of the polyline closure, on $4$ strands, of the braid word
$\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^{2}$
for the Conway knot.

articles.title: Closed unit disk in the plane
articles.statement:
The closed unit Euclidean disk
$\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \mid x^2 + y^2 \le 1\}$, the source of the
parametrization of a slicing disk.

The disk and its boundary circle are written out by the equations $x^2 + y^2 \le 1$ and
$x^2 + y^2 = 1$ rather than as the closed unit ball and unit sphere of $\mathbb{R} \times
\mathbb{R}$. The product carries the sup norm, so that ball would be the square $[-1, 1]^2$ and
that sphere its boundary, which has corners. At a corner, no smooth map with injective
derivative can match a corner-free smooth knot as its boundary, so slice disks parametrized by
the square cannot exist, and every knot would fail to be smoothly slice.

articles.title: Existence of non-isotopic knots
articles.statement:
There are two oriented smooth knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ in
$\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient-isotopic.

## Sources

- Classical; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_invariant. Problem `exists_nonisotopic_knots` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Non-isotopic two-component links exist
articles.statement:
There exist two oriented smooth two-component
links $L_1$ and $L_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient isotopic as oriented links with
ordered components: no ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries the first component of $L_1$ to
the first component of $L_2$ and the second component of $L_1$ to the second component of $L_2$,
each up to an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle.

## Sources

- Classical; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linking_number. Problem `exists_nonisotopic_link` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Smooth representative of a PL knot
articles.statement:
A smooth knot $J$ is a smooth representative of
the piecewise-linear knot $K$ if the image of $J$ and the image of $K$ are unoriented
topologically ambient isotopic in $\mathbb{R}^3$: some topological ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfies $H_1(\operatorname{im} J) = \operatorname{im} K$.

When the polyline $K$ is simple, both curves are tame, and this agrees with the usual relation
of having the same smooth/PL knot type.

articles.title: Identity reparametrization of the circle
articles.statement:
The identity circle reparametrization has
lift and inverse lift both equal to the identity map of $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Identity ambient isotopy
articles.statement:
The identity ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ has forward
and inverse families $H_t$ and $G_t$ equal to the identity map of $\mathbb{R}^3$ for every
time $t$.

articles.title: Image of a PL knot
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a PL knot with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$. Its image is
the subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ traced by the closed polyline through these vertices: the image of the
half-open interval $[0, n)$ under the parametrization that sends $k + \alpha$, for an integer
$0 \le k < n$ and a real $0 \le \alpha < 1$, to $(1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$, with indices
taken modulo $n$.

articles.title: Local flatness at a boundary point
articles.statement:
Let $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ and
$D : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$. Write $\Delta = \{(x, y) : x^2 + y^2 \le 1\}$
for the closed unit disk, $H = \{(p, s) : s \ge 0\}$ for the closed upper half-space, and
$P = \{((p_1, p_2, p_3), s) : p_2 = p_3 = 0,\ s \ge 0\}$ for the model half-plane. The image
$D(\Delta)$ is locally flat at $q$ in the boundary sense if there is a homeomorphism $h : U \to V$
between open subsets $U$, $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ such that $q \in U$,
$h(U \cap H) = V \cap H$ and $h(U \cap D(\Delta)) = V \cap P$.

The chart is open in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ rather than in $H$: when the last coordinate
of $q$ is $0$, every open neighbourhood of $q$ leaves $H$.

articles.title: Local flatness at an interior point
articles.statement:
Let $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ and
$D : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$. Write $\Delta = \{(x, y) : x^2 + y^2 \le 1\}$
for the closed unit disk and $P = \{((p_1, p_2, p_3), s) : p_2 = p_3 = 0\}$ for the model plane.
The image $D(\Delta)$ is locally flat at $q$ in the interior sense if there is a homeomorphism
$h : U \to V$ between open subsets $U$, $V$ of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ such that $q \in U$
and $h(U \cap D(\Delta)) = V \cap P$.

articles.title: Simple PL knot
articles.statement:
A PL knot $K$ with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ is simple if its closed
polyline parametrization, which sends $k + \alpha$, for an integer $0 \le k < n$ and a real
$0 \le \alpha < 1$, to $(1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$ (indices modulo $n$), is injective on
the half-open interval $[0, n)$.

Equivalently, the polyline is a simple closed curve: all vertices are distinct, non-adjacent
edges are disjoint, and adjacent edges meet only at their shared vertex.

articles.title: Isotopy of parametrized links
articles.statement:
Two parametrized links in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with $n$
components $\gamma^1_i$ and $\gamma^2_i$ ($i < n$) are isotopic (oriented, labeled ambient
isotopy) if there are a single smooth ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with forward family
$H_t$ and, for each $i < n$, an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle with
lift $f_i$, such that $H_1(\gamma^1_i(t)) = \gamma^2_i(f_i(t))$ for every $i < n$ and every
$t \in \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Ambient isotopy of oriented knots
articles.statement:
Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be oriented knots, each given by
its $2\pi$-periodic parametrization. They are ambient-isotopic if there are a smooth ambient
isotopy $(\Phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and an orientation-preserving smooth
reparametrization $\sigma$ of the circle such that $\Phi_1(K_1(t)) = K_2(\sigma(t))$ for every real
$t$. Here an orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle is a smooth, strictly
increasing bijection $\sigma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth inverse such that
$\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for every $t$.

articles.title: Ambient isotopy of oriented two-component links
articles.statement:
Let $L = (K, J)$ and $L' = (K', J')$ be
oriented two-component links, each knot given by its $2\pi$-periodic parametrization. Then $L$
and $L'$ are ambient-isotopic if there are a smooth ambient isotopy $(\Phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$
of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and orientation-preserving smooth reparametrizations $\sigma$, $\tau$ of the
circle such that $\Phi_1(K(t)) = K'(\sigma(t))$ and $\Phi_1(J(t)) = J'(\tau(t))$ for every real
$t$. Here an orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle is a smooth, strictly
increasing bijection $\sigma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth inverse such that
$\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for every $t$.

articles.title: Isotopy of parametrized knots
articles.statement:
Two parametrized knots $\gamma_1, \gamma_2$ in
$\mathbb{R}^3$ are isotopic (oriented ambient isotopy) if there are a smooth ambient isotopy
of $\mathbb{R}^3$ with forward family $H_t$ and an orientation-preserving reparametrization
of the circle with lift $f$ such that $H_1(\gamma_1(t)) = \gamma_2(f(t))$ for every
$t \in \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Iterated braid-closure passes
articles.statement:
For a braid word $w$, a number $f$ of remaining passes and
a traversal state $S$, the iteration returns $S$ when $f = 0$. When $f > 0$ it applies one pass
of $w$ to $S$, obtaining a state $S'$; it returns $S'$ if the strand position of $S'$ is $1$, and
otherwise iterates on $S'$ with $f - 1$ passes remaining.

The bound $f$ guarantees termination. The braid closure on $n$ strands uses $f = n$, since at
most $n$ distinct strand positions are visited.

articles.title: Knots are the same as parametrized knots
articles.statement:
Sending a knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to the
parametrized knot with the same parametrization is a bijection from knots to parametrized knots,
whose inverse sends a parametrized knot to the knot with the same parametrization.

articles.title: Isotopy of knots agrees with isotopy of parametrized knots
articles.statement:
For all knots $K_1$ and
$K_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $K_1$ and $K_2$ are ambient isotopic if and only if the parametrized knots
with the same parametrizations as $K_1$ and $K_2$ are ambient isotopic as parametrized knots.

articles.title: Oriented smooth knot
articles.statement:
An oriented smooth knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a smooth map
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is $2\pi$-periodic, injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, and an
immersion, meaning $\gamma'(t) \ne 0$ for every real $t$. The orientation is the one induced by
the parametrization.

articles.title: Point from three coordinates
articles.statement:
For real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$, this is the point
$(x, y, z)$ of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.

articles.title: Model half-plane
articles.statement:
The model half-plane is the set of pairs $((p_1, p_2, p_3), s)$ in
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ with $p_2 = p_3 = 0$ and $s \ge 0$. It is a copy of the closed
half-plane $\mathbb{R} \times [0, \infty)$, with coordinates $p_1$ and $s$, lying in the upper
half-space $s \ge 0$.

It is the local model for boundary local flatness of a properly embedded disk.

articles.title: Model interior $2$-plane
articles.statement:
The model interior $2$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$
is the set of points $((x_1, x_2, x_3), t)$ with $x_2 = x_3 = 0$, where $x_1$ and $t$ are
arbitrary. It is the local model for interior local flatness of an embedded $2$-disk.

articles.title: Euclidean ambient isotopies as Conway-knot ambient isotopies
articles.statement:
A smooth ambient isotopy
of Euclidean 3-space in the sense of parametrized links, given by maps
$H_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$ with $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ smooth
and $H_0 = \mathrm{id}$, and maps $G_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with
$(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ smooth and $G_t \circ H_t = H_t \circ G_t = \mathrm{id}$ for every $t$,
is sent to the ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the sense of the Conway knot statements with
the same forward family $H$ and inverse family $G$.

articles.title: Euclidean circle reparametrizations as Conway-knot ones
articles.statement:
A circle reparametrization in
the sense of parametrized links, given by a smooth strictly increasing map
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth two-sided inverse $g$ such that
$f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, is sent to the
orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization of the circle in the sense of the Conway knot
statements with the same lift $f$ and inverse lift $g$.

articles.title: Parametrized knots as knots
articles.statement:
A parametrized knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$, given by a smooth
$2\pi$-periodic immersion $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is injective on
$[0, 2\pi)$, is sent to the knot with the same parametrization $\gamma$.

articles.title: Labeled two-component links as two-component links
articles.statement:
A labeled parametrized link with
two components $0$ and $1$ is sent to the two-component link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose first
component is the knot with the same parametrization as component $0$ and whose second component
is the knot with the same parametrization as component $1$.

articles.title: One pass of the braid closure
articles.statement:
Let $w$ be a braid word (a list of integers) of length $m$.
Starting from a traversal state, one pass applies the letters of $w$ in order as crossings, the
$k$-th letter (counting from $0$) occupying the slab $-(k+1) \le z \le -k$; this moves the state
to a strand position $p$ and appends the crossing vertices. It then appends the closure arc: the
vertices $(p, 100, -m)$ and $(p, 100, 0)$, followed by $(p, 0, 0)$ unless $p = 1$. The resulting
state has position $p$ and the extended vertex list.

When $p = 1$ the vertex $(1, 0, 0)$ is left out because the polyline starts there, so the closure
arc already returns to its first vertex.

articles.title: Parametrized knot
articles.statement:
An oriented parametrized smooth knot in Euclidean 3-space is a
$C^\infty$ curve $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is $2\pi$-periodic
($\gamma(t + 2\pi) = \gamma(t)$ for all $t$), injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, and an immersion
($\gamma'(t) \neq 0$ for all $t$).

articles.title: Parametrized link
articles.statement:
An oriented labeled parametrized smooth link with $n$ components
in Euclidean 3-space is a family $(\gamma_i)_{i < n}$ of parametrized knots whose traces
$\gamma_i(\mathbb{R})$ are pairwise disjoint.

articles.title: Parametrization of a closed polyline
articles.statement:
Let $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ be a list of $n \ge 1$
points of $\mathbb{R}^3$. The polyline curve is the $n$-periodic map
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with $\gamma(k + \alpha) = (1 - \alpha) v_k + \alpha v_{k+1}$
for integers $0 \le k < n$ and reals $0 \le \alpha < 1$, where indices are taken modulo $n$ (so
$v_n = v_0$). For the empty list the curve is constantly $0$.

articles.title: PL knot (closed polyline)
articles.statement:
A PL knot is a list $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ of points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ with $n \ge 3$, viewed as the vertices, in order, of the closed polyline with edges
from $v_i$ to $v_{i+1}$ for $i < n - 1$ and from $v_{n-1}$ back to $v_0$.

Simplicity of the polyline (that it is an embedded closed curve) is not part of the data; it is
imposed as a separate condition.

articles.title: Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$
articles.statement:
The ambient space of the knots here is $\mathbb{R}^3$ with
its standard Euclidean inner product.

articles.title: Reflection in the $xy$-plane
articles.statement:
The reflection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ through the $xy$-plane is
the map $(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y, -z)$.

articles.title: Ropelength of a parametrized knot
articles.statement:
The ropelength of a parametrized knot $K$ is the
ropelength of the one-component parametrized link determined by $K$: the infimum, in
$[0, \infty]$, of the ropelength ratios of all one-component parametrized links that are
isotopic to the one-component link of $K$.

articles.title: Ropelength is an isotopy invariant
articles.statement:
Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be parametrized links with $n$
components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ (by an oriented, labeled ambient isotopy), then the
ropelength of $L_1$ equals the ropelength of $L_2$.

articles.title: Ropelength is at most the ratio of any isotopic link
articles.statement:
Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized
links with $n$ components. If $L'$ is isotopic to $L$, then the ropelength of $L$ is at most
the ropelength ratio of $L'$.

articles.title: Ropelength is at most the ropelength ratio
articles.statement:
For every parametrized link $L$ with $n$
components, the ropelength of $L$ is at most the ropelength ratio of $L$.

articles.title: Ropelength ratio of a parametrized link
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$, the ropelength
ratio of $L$ is its total contour length divided by the thickness of its trace (the union of the
images of its components), a value in $[0, \infty]$ computed with the division of $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Ropelength of a parametrized link
articles.statement:
For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the
ropelength of $L$ is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the ropelength ratios of all parametrized
links $L'$ with $n$ components that are isotopic to $L$. It is the ropelength of the oriented,
labeled ambient-isotopy type of $L$.

articles.title: Smoothly slice (PL knot version)
articles.statement:
A PL knot $K$ is smoothly slice if there is a smooth
knot $J$ that is smoothly slice and is a smooth representative of $K$: for some topological
ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$, the map $H_1$ carries the image of $J$ onto the image
(trace) of the polyline $K$.

Piccirillo's theorem that the Conway knot is not smoothly slice is stated with this notion.

articles.title: Smoothly slice (smooth knot version)
articles.statement:
Let
$\Delta = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : x^2 + y^2 \le 1\}$ be the closed unit disk and
$C = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : x^2 + y^2 = 1\}$ its boundary circle. A smooth knot $K$ is
smoothly slice if there is a smooth ($C^\infty$) map $f : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times
\mathbb{R}$ such that $f$ is injective on $\Delta$; for every $p \in \Delta$ the last coordinate
of $f(p)$ is nonnegative, and it is $0$ exactly when $p \in C$; the derivative of $f$ at every
point of $\Delta$ is injective; and the image of $C$ under the $\mathbb{R}^3$-component of $f$
is the image of $K$.

articles.title: Braid closure traversal state
articles.statement:
A traversal state for tracing the closure of a braid
consists of the current strand position, a natural number, and the list of points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ accumulated so far, in order, as vertices of the polyline.

articles.title: Inverse circle reparametrization
articles.statement:
The inverse of a circle reparametrization with lift
$f$ and inverse lift $f^{-1}$ is the circle reparametrization whose lift is $f^{-1}$ and whose
inverse lift is $f$.

articles.title: Inverse ambient isotopy
articles.statement:
The inverse of an ambient isotopy with forward family $(H_t)$ and
inverse family $(H_t^{-1})$ is the ambient isotopy whose forward family is $(H_t^{-1})$ and whose
inverse family is $(H_t)$; at each time $t$ it is the inverse diffeomorphism of $H_t$.

articles.title: Conway-knot ambient isotopies as Euclidean ambient isotopies
articles.statement:
An ambient isotopy of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ in the sense of the Conway knot statements, given by maps
$H_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$ with $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ smooth
and $H_0 = \mathrm{id}$, and maps $G_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with
$(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$ smooth and $G_t \circ H_t = H_t \circ G_t = \mathrm{id}$ for every $t$,
is sent to the smooth ambient isotopy of Euclidean 3-space, in the sense of parametrized links,
with the same forward family $H$ and inverse family $G$.

articles.title: Conway-knot circle reparametrizations as Euclidean ones
articles.statement:
An orientation-preserving smooth
reparametrization of the circle in the sense of the Conway knot statements, given by a smooth
strictly increasing map $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with smooth two-sided inverse $g$ such that
$f(t + 2\pi) = f(t) + 2\pi$ and $g(t + 2\pi) = g(t) + 2\pi$ for all $t$, is sent to the circle
reparametrization, in the sense of parametrized links, with the same lift $f$ and inverse
lift $g$.

articles.title: Isotopic knots give isotopic one-component links
articles.statement:
If $K_1$ and $K_2$ are parametrized
knots and $K_1$ is isotopic to $K_2$, then the one-component parametrized link of $K_1$ is
isotopic to the one-component parametrized link of $K_2$.

articles.title: Parametrized knot as a one-component link
articles.statement:
A parametrized knot $K$ determines the
parametrized link with one component, whose single component is $K$; the pairwise disjointness
condition holds trivially.

articles.title: Knots as parametrized knots
articles.statement:
A knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$, given by a smooth $2\pi$-periodic
immersion $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, is sent to the
parametrized knot with the same parametrization $\gamma$.

articles.title: Two-component links as labeled links
articles.statement:
A two-component link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with first
component $K$ and second component $L$ is sent to the labeled parametrized link with two
components whose component $0$ is the parametrized knot with the same parametrization as $K$ and
whose component $1$ is the parametrized knot with the same parametrization as $L$.

articles.title: Topological ambient isotopy
articles.statement:
A topological ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a family of
maps $H_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$, indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}$, together with a family
$G_t : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $(t, x) \mapsto H_t(x)$ and $(t, x) \mapsto G_t(x)$
are continuous, $G_t$ is a two-sided inverse of $H_t$ for every $t$ (so each $H_t$ is a
homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$), and $H_0$ is the identity.

The time domain is all of $\mathbb{R}$, but only $H_0$ and $H_1$ matter for the isotopy
relation.

articles.title: Topologically slice (PL knot version)
articles.statement:
A PL knot $K$ is topologically slice if there is a
smooth knot $J$ that is a smooth representative of $K$, meaning that the image of $J$ and the image
of $K$ are unoriented topologically ambient isotopic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3$, and such that $J$
is topologically slice as a smooth knot.

articles.title: Topologically slice (smooth knot version)
articles.statement:
Write points of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$
as $(x, s)$ with $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$. Let $H = \{(x, s) : s \ge 0\}$ be the closed upper
half-space, $P = \{(x, s) : x_2 = x_3 = 0\}$ the model plane and $P_+ = P \cap H$ the model
half-plane, and let $D^2 = \{(a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : a^2 + b^2 \le 1\}$ and
$S^1 = \{(a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : a^2 + b^2 = 1\}$. A smooth knot $K$ is topologically slice if
there is a continuous map $D : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$, injective on
$D^2$, such that: for every $p \in D^2$ the last coordinate of $D(p)$ is nonnegative, and it is
$0$ exactly when $p \in S^1$; for every $p \in D^2 \setminus S^1$ there is a homeomorphism
$h : U \to V$ between open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ with $D(p) \in U$ and
$h(U \cap D(D^2)) = V \cap P$; for every $p \in S^1$ there is such a homeomorphism with
$D(p) \in U$, $h(U \cap H) = V \cap H$ and $h(U \cap D(D^2)) = V \cap P_+$; and the image of
$S^1$ under the $\mathbb{R}^3$-component of $D$ is the image of $K$.

articles.title: Total contour length of a parametrized link
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a parametrized link in
Euclidean 3-space with components $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$, each a $2\pi$-periodic curve.
The total contour length of $L$ is the sum over all components $\gamma_i$ of the contour
length of $\gamma_i$ on one period $[0, 2\pi]$. It is a value in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Trace of a parametrized link
articles.statement:
The trace of a parametrized link $L$ in Euclidean 3-space
is the union of the images of its component curves: the set of all points $\gamma(t)$, where
$\gamma$ is a component of $L$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Two-component link isotopy agrees with labeled link isotopy
articles.statement:
Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be
oriented two-component smooth links in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and regard each as an oriented labeled
smooth link with two components, whose component $0$ is its first component and whose
component $1$ is its second. Then $L_1$ and $L_2$ are ambient isotopic, meaning that a single
smooth ambient isotopy carries each component of $L_1$ onto the corresponding component of
$L_2$ up to orientation-preserving reparametrizations of the circle, if and only if the
associated labeled links are ambient isotopic.

articles.title: Two-component link
articles.statement:
An oriented two-component smooth link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a pair
$(K, L)$ of oriented smooth knots whose images in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are disjoint.

articles.title: Topological ambient isotopy of subsets
articles.statement:
Two subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ are
unoriented topologically ambient isotopic if there is a topological ambient isotopy $(H_t)$ of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ whose time-one map carries $A$ onto $B$, that is, $H_1(A) = B$.

"Unoriented" because this is a set-level relation that forgets any parametrization.

articles.title: Closed upper half-space
articles.statement:
The closed upper half-space in $\mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$
is the set $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, \infty)$ of points $(x, s)$ with $s \ge 0$.

We identify $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, \infty)$ with $B^4 \setminus \{\mathrm{pt}\}$, so slice
disks live here.

articles.title: Oesper's determinant formula for three-strand weaving knots
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ be an integer,
let $F_i$ be the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$), let
$C_j = \sum_{i=1}^{j} (-1)^{i+1} F_i$ for $j \ge 0$, and let $M$ be the $3 \times 3$ integer
matrix with rows $(2, -1, 0)$, $(0, 0, 1)$ and $(-1, 0, 2)$. Then the absolute value of the
determinant of the $2 \times 2$ matrix obtained from $M^k - I$ by deleting its first row and
first column equals $-(C_{2k-2} + 1) C_{2k} + C_{2k-1}^2$.

Here $M$ is the base-word matrix of the spiral knot $S(3, k, (1, -1))$, which is the
three-strand weaving knot $W(k, 3)$, and the left-hand side is the determinant of this knot:
the cofactor minors of $M^k - I$ agree up to sign, so taking the absolute value gives the
nonnegative knot determinant.

## Sources

- Seong Ju Kim, Ryan Stees, and Laura Taalman, "Sequences of Spiral Knot Determinants", Journal of Integer Sequences 19 (2016), Article 16.1.4, lines 409-412: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL19/Stees/stees4.tex The formula is attributed to L. Oesper, "p-colorings of weaving knots" (preprint).

articles.title: Quadrisecant of a knot
articles.statement:
A knot $K$ with parametrization
$\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ has a quadrisecant when there are pairwise distinct
reals $t_0, t_1, t_2, t_3 \in [0, 2\pi)$, a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^3$, a nonzero vector
$v \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3$ such that $\gamma(t_i) = p + a_i v$ for each
$i$, that is, the four points $\gamma(t_i)$ lie on one line.

articles.title: Unknotted knot
articles.statement:
A knot $K$ is unknotted when there is a knot $J$ whose parametrization is
the standard circle $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$ such that $K$ is ambient-isotopic to $J$ as
an oriented knot.

articles.title: Period
articles.statement: The period is the real number $2\pi$.

articles.title: Quadrisecant theorem (Pannwitz–Kuperberg)
articles.statement:
Every smooth knot $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is
not unknotted has a quadrisecant.

## Sources

- E. Pannwitz (1933); G. Kuperberg, *Quadrisecants of knots and links*, J. Knot Theory Ramif. 3 (1994). Knill, §161. Problem `smooth_knot_has_quadrisecant` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Standard circle
articles.statement:
The standard circle is the curve $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by
$t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$, the unit circle in the $xy$-plane.

articles.title: Extended circumradius of a triangle
articles.statement:
Let $p, q, r$ be points of Euclidean 3-space and
let $T$ be a triangle in Euclidean 3-space whose vertices, in order, are $p$, $q$ and $r$. Then
the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ equals the circumradius of $T$.

articles.title: Collinear points have infinite extended circumradius
articles.statement:
If $p, q, r$ are points of
Euclidean 3-space and the set $\{p, q, r\}$ is collinear, then the extended circumradius of
$(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.

articles.title: Equal first two points give infinite extended circumradius
articles.statement:
If $p, q, r$ are points of
Euclidean 3-space with $p = q$, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.

A triple with coincident points is treated as degenerate, not as having radius zero.

articles.title: Extended circumradius is invariant under reversal
articles.statement:
For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean
3-space, the extended circumradius of $(r, q, p)$ equals the extended circumradius of
$(p, q, r)$.

articles.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the first two points
articles.statement:
For all points $p, q, r$ of
Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(q, p, r)$ equals the extended circumradius of
$(p, q, r)$.

articles.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the last two points
articles.statement:
For all points $p, q, r$ of
Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, r, q)$ equals the extended circumradius of
$(p, q, r)$.

articles.title: Translation invariance of the extended circumradius
articles.statement:
For every vector $v$ and all points
$p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(v + p, v + q, v + r)$ equals the
extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.

articles.title: Extended circumradius of three points
articles.statement:
For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the
extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is the following value in $[0, \infty]$. If $p, q, r$ are
affinely independent, it is the circumradius of the triangle with vertices $p$, $q$ and $r$.
Otherwise, that is, when the three points are collinear (in particular when two of them
coincide), it is $\infty$.

This matches the convention that collinear points determine a circle of infinite radius.

articles.title: Contour length of a $C^1$ curve
articles.statement:
Let $a \le b$ be real numbers and let $\gamma$ be a
map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space that is continuously differentiable on $[a, b]$.
Then the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ equals
$\int_a^b \lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert \, dt$.

articles.title: Contour length
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space and let
$a, b$ be real numbers. The contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the total variation of
$\gamma$ on $[a, b]$: the supremum, over all finite sequences $t_0 \le t_1 \le \dots \le t_n$
of points of $[a, b]$, of $\sum_{i < n} \lVert \gamma(t_{i+1}) - \gamma(t_i) \rVert$. It is a
value in $[0, \infty]$.

For continuously differentiable curves it equals the integral of the speed.

articles.title: Alternating link types have finite crossing number
articles.statement:
If an
oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an alternating
diagram, then its crossing number is finite: the alternating
representative is itself a regular projection.

articles.title: Alternating link types have a natural-number crossing number
articles.statement:
If an oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an
alternating diagram, then its crossing number equals some natural
number $k$.

articles.title: Zero is an admissible alternating constant
articles.statement:
The constant
$c = 0$ is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality.

articles.title: Admissible constants for the tight alternating knot inequality
articles.statement:
A real number $c$ is admissible when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n$ and
every oriented labeled link type with $n$ components that admits an
alternating diagram and whose crossing number is a natural number $k$,
the ropelength of the type is at least $c k$.

The restriction to finite crossing number excludes no such type: the
alternating representative is itself a regular projection, so every
link type admitting an alternating diagram has finite crossing
number.

articles.title: Zero is an admissible tight-knot constant
articles.statement:
The real number $0$ is admissible for the
tight-knot inequality between the ropelength and the crossing number of link types.

articles.title: Admissible constants for the tight-knot inequality
articles.statement:
A real number $c$ is admissible for
the tight-knot inequality when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every parametrized
link $L$ with $n$ components and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the crossing number of $L$
equals $k$, the ropelength of $L$ is at least $c \, k^{3/4}$, the inequality being read in
$[0, \infty]$. Here the crossing number and the ropelength of $L$ are those of its oriented
labeled ambient-isotopy type.

Link types of infinite crossing number, that is, types none of whose representatives admits a
regular projection, impose no constraint.

articles.title: Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot constant
articles.statement:
**Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot
constant.** Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight
alternating knot inequality is at most the tight alternating knot
constant.

articles.title: Admissible constants are bounded by the tight knot constant
articles.statement:
Let $C_{22a}$ be the tight
knot constant. Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies
$c \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.

articles.title: Admissibility passes to smaller nonnegative constants
articles.statement:
If a real number $c$ is admissible
for the tight-knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with $0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is
admissible for the tight-knot inequality as well.

articles.title: Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among nonnegative reals
articles.statement:
**Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among
nonnegative reals.** If a real number $c$ is admissible for the tight
alternating knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with
$0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is admissible as well.

articles.title: Euclidean 3-space
articles.statement: The space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm.

articles.title: Ropelength ratio
articles.statement:
For a curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a, b$, the
ropelength ratio of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ divided by
the thickness of the trace $\gamma([a, b])$. The quotient is taken in $[0, \infty]$, where
$c / 0 = \infty$ for $c \ne 0$, $0 / 0 = 0$ and $c / \infty = 0$.

The ropelength of a knot or link type is a further infimum of this ratio over the curves
representing the type.

articles.title: Thickness is antitone
articles.statement:
If $s \subseteq t$ are sets in Euclidean 3-space, then the
thickness of $t$ is at most the thickness of $s$: enlarging a set can only add triples and
hence can only decrease the infimum.

articles.title: Thickness of the empty set
articles.statement:
The empty subset of Euclidean 3-space has thickness
$\infty$, as an empty infimum in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Thickness is at most every circumradius
articles.statement:
For every set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space and all
points $p, q, r \in s$, the thickness of $s$ is at most the extended circumradius of
$p, q, r$.

articles.title: Thickness of a single point
articles.statement:
For every point $p$ of Euclidean 3-space, the set $\{p\}$
has thickness $\infty$: its only triple $(p, p, p)$ is degenerate.

articles.title: Thickness
articles.statement:
The thickness of a set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space is the infimum, in
$[0, \infty]$, of the extended circumradii of $(p, q, r)$ over all points $p, q, r \in s$.
Since the extended circumradius of three collinear points (in particular of three points two of
which coincide) is $\infty$, this is also the infimum over the triples of pairwise distinct
points of $s$.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the tight alternating knot constant
articles.statement:
For every
extended real number $b$, the tight alternating knot constant is at
most $b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is admissible for
the tight alternating knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.

articles.title: Tight alternating knot constant
articles.statement:
The tight alternating knot
constant $C_{22b} = b_0$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals,
of the set of real numbers $c$ admissible for the tight alternating
knot inequality: those $c \ge 0$ such that every link type $K$ that
admits an alternating diagram and has finite crossing number
$\mathrm{Cr}(K)$ has ropelength $\mathrm{L}(K) \ge c\,\mathrm{Cr}(K)$.
The supremum is not assumed to be attained.

articles.title: Upper bounds for the tight knot constant
articles.statement:
For every extended real number $b$, the tight
knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies $C_{22a} \le b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is
admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.

This is the characteristic rule for proving upper bounds on the tight knot constant without
unfolding its definition as a supremum.

articles.title: Tight knot constant
articles.statement:
The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ is the supremum, taken in the
extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ that are admissible for the
tight-knot inequality $\mathrm{ropelength} \ge c \cdot (\text{crossing number})^{3/4}$ on link
types. The supremum is not assumed to be attained.

articles.title: Triangle on three affinely independent points
articles.statement:
For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space
whose ordered triple $(p, q, r)$ is affinely independent, the triangle in Euclidean 3-space with
vertices $p$, $q$, $r$, in that order.

articles.title: Ordered triple of points
articles.statement:
For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the family indexed by
$\{0, 1, 2\}$ that sends $0 \mapsto p$, $1 \mapsto q$ and $2 \mapsto r$.

articles.title: The tight alternating knot constant is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The tight
alternating knot constant, an extended real number, is at least $0$.

articles.title: The tight knot constant is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies
$0 \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.

articles.title: The Conway knot polyline is a simple closed curve
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be the Conway knot $11n34$,
realized as a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the braid closure of a 4-strand braid word for
it), and let $N$ be its number of vertices. The periodic piecewise-linear parametrization of $K$,
which traverses each edge in unit time, is injective on the interval $[0, N)$.

Equivalently, the vertices of $K$ are distinct, non-adjacent edges are disjoint, and adjacent
edges meet only at their shared vertex.

## Sources

- https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02923. Problem `conway_knot_not_smoothly_slice` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Conway knot is not smoothly slice (Piccirillo)
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be the Conway knot $11n34$,
realized as a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$. There is no smooth knot $J$, that is, a smooth
$2\pi$-periodic map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with nowhere vanishing derivative that is
injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, with both of the following properties: some topological ambient isotopy
of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries the image of $J$ onto the image of $K$; and there is a smooth map
$D \colon \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ that is injective with injective
derivative on the closed unit disk $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$, takes $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ into the
half-space $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, \infty)$, takes a point of $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ to height
$0$ exactly when it lies on the unit circle, and whose $\mathbb{R}^3$-component maps the unit
circle onto the image of $J$.

## Sources

- https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02923. Problem `conway_knot_not_smoothly_slice` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Conway knot is topologically slice
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be the PL knot traced by the braid closure
on $4$ strands of the braid word
$\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^2$
for the Conway knot 11n34. Then $K$ is topologically slice: there is a smooth knot $J$ whose
image is unoriented topologically ambient isotopic in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to the image of $K$, and $J$
is topologically slice.

This follows from Freedman's theorem that every knot with trivial Alexander polynomial is
topologically slice, since the Conway knot has $\Delta_K(t) = 1$.

## Sources

- Freedman, *The topology of four-dimensional manifolds*, J. Diff. Geom. 17 (1982). See also Freedman-Quinn, *Topology of 4-Manifolds*, Princeton 1990. Problem `conway_knot_topologically_slice` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: A topologically slice knot that is not smoothly slice
articles.statement:
There is a PL knot $K$ (a closed
polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with at least three vertices, not required to be simple) that is
topologically slice but not smoothly slice. Here $K$ is smoothly (respectively topologically)
slice when some smooth knot whose image is topologically ambient isotopic to the image of $K$
bounds a smooth (respectively locally flat) properly embedded $2$-disk in
$\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, \infty)$.

## Sources

- Casson, 1980s (unpublished); Akbulut-Matveyev, *A convex decomposition theorem for 4-manifolds*, IMRN 1998. See also Hedden-Kirk-Livingston, *Non-slice linear combinations of algebraic knots*, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 14 (2012). Problem `exists_topologically_slice_not_smoothly_slice` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Ambient Euclidean space
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the ambient space is the real
Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$, with coordinates indexed by $0, \dots, n-1$ and
the Euclidean norm.

articles.title: Annulus theorem in dimension four
articles.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be locally flat embedded $3$-spheres
in $\mathbb{R}^4$, that is, continuous injective locally flat maps $S^3 \to \mathbb{R}^4$ from the
unit sphere. Suppose that the images of $f$ and $g$ are disjoint and that the image of $g$ lies
in the inside of the image of $f$, the set of points off the image of $f$ whose connected
component in its complement is bounded. Then the region between $f$ and $g$, the closure of the
inside of the image of $f$ minus the inside of the image of $g$, is homeomorphic to
$S^3 \times [0, 1]$.

## Sources

- F. Quinn, *Ends of maps III: dimensions 4 and 5*, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982), building on M. H. Freedman, *The topology of four-dimensional manifolds*, J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982). Problem `annulus_theorem_dim_four` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Annulus theorem in dimensions at least five
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 5$ and let $f$ and $g$ be locally
flat embedded $(n-1)$-spheres in $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is, continuous injective locally flat maps
$S^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ from the unit sphere. Suppose that the images of $f$ and $g$ are
disjoint and that the image of $g$ lies in the inside of the image of $f$, the set of points off
the image of $f$ whose connected component in its complement is bounded. Then the region between
$f$ and $g$, the closure of the inside of the image of $f$ minus the inside of the image of $g$,
is homeomorphic to $S^{n-1} \times [0, 1]$.

## Sources

- R. C. Kirby, *Stable homeomorphisms and the annulus conjecture*, Ann. of Math. 89 (1969). Problem `annulus_theorem_high_dim` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Locally flat embedded sphere
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 1$, a locally flat embedded $(n-1)$-sphere in
$\mathbb{R}^n$ is a map $f : S^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ from the unit sphere that is continuous,
injective and locally flat.

articles.title: Inside of a set
articles.statement:
For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the inside of $S$ is the set of
points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in the complement $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus S$ is
bounded.

For the image of a locally flat embedded sphere, this is the open ball it bounds.

articles.title: Locally flat maps of the sphere
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be the
unit sphere and let $H = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : x_0 = 0\}$ be the model hyperplane. A map
$c : S^{n-1} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is locally flat if for every point $p \in S^{n-1}$ there are open
sets $U, V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with $c(p) \in U$ and a homeomorphism $h : U \to V$ such that
$h(U \cap c(S^{n-1})) = V \cap H$.

articles.title: Model hyperplane
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 1$, the model hyperplane in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of
points $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ whose first coordinate $x_0$ is $0$. It is the local model for
a locally flat embedded sphere.

articles.title: Region between two flat spheres
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $f$ and $g$ be locally flat
embedded $(n-1)$-spheres in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The region between $f$ and $g$ is the closure of the
inside of the image of $f$ with the inside of the image of $g$ removed, where the inside of a set
$S$ is the set of points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in $\mathbb{R}^n \setminus S$ is
bounded.

articles.title: Unit sphere in Euclidean space
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the unit sphere
$S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is the set of points of $\mathbb{R}^n$ at Euclidean distance $1$
from the origin.

articles.title: Existence of an aspherical integer homology 4-sphere
articles.statement:
There is a closed connected
topological 4-manifold $M$ that is aspherical, meaning that for every $k \ge 2$ and every point
$x \in M$ the homotopy group $\pi_k(M, x)$ is trivial, and that is an integer homology 4-sphere,
meaning that for every $k \ge 0$ the integral singular homology $H_k(M; \mathbb{Z})$ is isomorphic
to $H_k(S^4; \mathbb{Z})$, where $S^4$ is the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^5$.

## Sources

- J. G. Ratcliffe and S. T. Tschantz, *Some examples of aspherical 4-manifolds that are homology 4-spheres*, arXiv:math/0312436 (2003), solving [Kir97, Problem 4.17]. Earlier, F. Luo constructed an aspherical rational homology 4-sphere (1988). Problem `aspherical_integer_homology_four_sphere` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Closed topological 4-manifold
articles.statement:
A closed topological 4-manifold is a nonempty, compact,
connected, Hausdorff, second-countable topological space $M$ together with an atlas of charts
covering $M$, each a homeomorphism from an open subset of $M$ onto an open subset of
$\mathbb{R}^4$ (charts are modelled on all of $\mathbb{R}^4$, not on a half-space, so $M$ has no
boundary).

No smoothness or compatibility between charts is required, so this is a topological, not
